content.text:
### Findings

**MEDIUM — `credit_string` silently mangles a credit when one part has no source, and the release is not counted incomplete.**
`src/discography/musicbrainz.rs:303-314`. The name falls back to `""` for a part with neither a credit-level `name` nor an `artist` entity, but the `joinphrase` is appended unconditionally. Scenario: payload `"artist-credit": [{"name":"Nu:Tone","joinphrase":" & "},{"joinphrase":" & "},{"name":"Stamina MC"}]` (an anonymous middle part) yields `"Nu:Tone && Stamina MC"`, which then becomes the Soulseek search artist and the staging folder name (`label_discover.rs:163-175` → `runner.rs:2770-2792`). A trailing anonymous part yields `"Nu:Tone &"` instead. This contradicts the function's own comment ("a part with neither source contributes nothing") and the round-3 requirement that such a part makes the release incomplete; only an *entirely* empty credit is rejected (`musicbrainz.rs:324-326`). Smallest fix: append `joinphrase` only when `name` is non-empty, and treat a part with no source as a reason to return `None` from `from_wire` (count it `incomplete`); add the missing unit test (no test covers an anonymous part, with or without a joinphrase).

**MEDIUM — the label entry point and the dispatch branch are completely untested.**
`src/runner.rs:2548-2585` (`run_label_discover_mode`) is never called by any test, and neither is the `labels.is_empty()` branch in `src/main.rs:606-621`. Grep shows the only references are `main.rs:614` and the definition. Consequences: (a) an inverted or wrong guard on `labels.is_empty()` would silently run the artist sweep instead of the label sweep and no test would fail — the clap test (`main.rs:899-935`) and the plan test (`mode.rs:1290-1305`) stop short of dispatch; (b) the label-specific preconditions (`discography.enabled`, `library.paths`, `staging::prepare`) are unexercised; (c) this code is uncovered for the project's 95% line-coverage gate. Smallest fix: one `#[tokio::test]` in `main.rs` that dispatches `ExecutionPlan::Discover { labels: vec![LabelRequest{..}], .. }` with empty `library.paths` and asserts the label-specific text "a label sweep needs a library to check what is present" (`runner.rs:2564`) — it fails today if the branch is ever inverted, because the artist branch says "needs a library to derive artists from".

**MEDIUM — the round-3 invariant "a malformed refusal cannot suppress a later corrected run" has no test.**
`src/discography/label.rs:1153-1177` asserts only `search_calls == 0`, `from_cache == false` and the reason. Nothing asserts that no `discography_failures` row was written for the key and that a subsequent valid input still resolves. The behaviour is correct today (`label.rs:328-340` returns before the only writer at `label.rs:422`), but the property the review round asked for is exactly the one a future refactor (e.g. moving the guard below the replay) would break with no red test. Smallest fix: after the refusal, assert `db.get_discography_failure(&input.cache_key()).unwrap().is_none()`, then run `Input::parse("<correct UUID>")` against the same DB and assert a `Catalogue`.

**LOW — a malformed value is reported as a MusicBrainz resolution failure.**
`src/discography/label.rs:331-336` returns `kind: DiscoveryFailure::Unresolved`, so `runner.rs:2693-2703` logs "label could not be resolved on MusicBrainz: …" for a value that provably never went to MusicBrainz, pushes it into `counters.unresolved`, and (with a second unresolved label) prints "pin … with discography.label_mbids" (`label_discover.rs:288-297`) — advice that cannot work, because the guard runs before the pin is read. Unreachable from the binary (`mode.rs:82-99` refuses it), so this is a library-caller contract blemish only.

**LOW — README overstates the malformed-UUID shape rule.**
`README.md:221`: "four hyphen-separated hexadecimal groups within three characters of a UUID's 32 digits". `looks_like_mbid` (`src/discography/label.rs:138-151`) requires exactly four hyphens / **five** groups (8-4-4-4-12) and a stripped length of `30..=34`, i.e. within **two** digits. The refusal message itself is correct ("8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits"); the parenthetical should match it.

**LOW — a label run cancelled before its first label prints an empty summary.**
`runner.rs:2620-2631` returns through `finish_label_run` before `labels_examined` is incremented, and every notice in `label_notices` is conditional (`label_discover.rs:261,273,280,315,345,361`), so the run emits zero summary lines. `discover_notices` deliberately avoids exactly this ("A run that examined no artist at all would be silent otherwise", `discover.rs:754-766`). Smallest fix: emit the "`N` of `M` label(s) examined" line unconditionally (it reads honestly as `0 of 1`), plus a unit test for the all-default `LabelCounters`.

**LOW — the label core function drops the preconditions its artist twin repeats.**
`run_label_discover_mode_with_provider` (`runner.rs:2590-2601`) starts at `let allowed = …`, while `run_discover_mode_with_provider` re-checks `discography.enabled` and `library.paths` (`runner.rs:3080-3089`) even though its public wrapper already did. No current bug, but the two core entry points now disagree about whether they are safe to call directly, and the next caller inherits a silent half-configured run.

**LOW — the label run summary is undocumented.**
The README documents the `discover:` notice format in several places but has no description of the `label:` lines emitted by `label_notices` (`label_discover.rs:258-370`), nor does the `--label` row (`README.md:221`) state that a label sweep requires `discography.enabled: true` and a non-empty `library.paths` — both are enforced at `runner.rs:2557-2567`.

### Note for the supervisor (cannot be run here)

Please run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and the coverage gate (`cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 95`) before merging: finding 2 is partly a coverage-gate risk and none of these gates was executable in this review.

########## B ##########
### Findings

1. **MEDIUM — missing cancellation tests for the new label sweep.**
   `src/runner.rs` label test block (~:7040-7700). The sweep has three cancellation-sensitive exits — the between-labels poll (src/runner.rs:2620-2631), the scan-cancelled `finish_label_run` (:2737-2742) and the download-loop break (:2783-2785) — and none is exercised. The crate already has three cancellation tests for artist-only mode (`a_cancelled_scan_stops_a_legacy_artist_only_run`, `a_cancelled_scan_stops_an_artist_only_run_without_processing_an_album`, `authoritative_cancellation_stops_iteration`). Concrete failure: a plausible refactor that folds the cancel `break` into the budget-exhausted branch would set `budget_reached_at` on a user-interrupted run — precisely the false "budget reached" notice the artist sweep carries a comment against (runner.rs:3305-3310) — and CI would stay green. Smallest fix: one test per exit — a client that flips a shared flag after the first search (the existing `CancelAfterFirstSearchClient` pattern) driving `run_label_discover_mode_with_provider`, asserting no "budget reached" notice, the honest examined line, and no staging claims; plus an `Err(Cancelled)` result from `index_from_paths` (needs a stubbed scanner or an `AtomicBool` pre-set to true).

2. **MEDIUM — the whole-library scan is paid (and can abort) for a run that can stage nothing.**
   `src/runner.rs:2719-2755`. Selection and counters are computed *before* the scan, but the scan is unconditional. When `selection.targets` is empty (all catalogues filtered out by `--release-type`, or bounded out by `--since`: a very plausible invocation — "sweep label X, but only EPs" or "--since 2024" on a label that stopped releasing in 1990), the run still performs its longest phase — the full tag-scanning walk — only to count `present = 0` for zero targets, and a scan failure (unreadable root, `Err` at :2748-2754) then turns a run with no possible work into a nonzero exit. Skipping the walk when `selection.targets.is_empty()` removes the waste and the spurious error with no honesty change: present/missing/eligible all stay truthful at zero. (No information is lost — `present` can only count targets, and there are none.)

3. **LOW — `credit_string` can append a dangling joinphrase for a pathological payload.**
   `src/discography/musicbrainz.rs:295-314`. An entry carrying a `joinphrase` but *neither* a credit-level name *nor* an artist entity contributes only its joinphrase, so a credit assembled from such entries can become e.g. `"feat. X"` — non-empty, so `from_wire` keeps the release and it is matched under a string that names no artist, rather than being counted incomplete. Unreachable with real MusicBrainz payloads (every credit entry always carries `artist`); the struct is already defensive, so defend the same corner: drop a part's joinphrase when the part contributed no name (or count any part with no source as making the release incomplete). File the same caveat for `{"artist": {}}` (entity present, empty name).

4. **LOW — README wording for the malformed-ID rule is ambiguous.**
   `README.md` (`--label` CLI row, diff around line 221): "a value hyphenated like a MusicBrainz ID that is not one (four hyphen-separated hexadecimal groups within three characters of a UUID's 32 digits)". `looks_like_mbid` (src/discography/label.rs:138-150) requires *four hyphens* separating *five* groups of hex digits; the parenthetical can be misread as four groups. The runtime message already says it precisely ("8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits"). Suggest "four hyphens separating five hexadecimal groups within three characters of a UUID's 32 digits".

5. **LOW — README does not say `discover.exclude_artists` applies to label sweeps.**
   `README.md` label paragraph/`--label` row. The code applies exclusion to credit keys and counts them (`label_targets(..., &config.discover.exclude_artists)`, src/runner.rs:2723; notice at label_discover.rs:330-333), and the committed spec documents it (spec line 151-152), but the README never mentions it for `--label`. One sentence ("`discover.exclude_artists` still applies to credits") closes it.

6. **LOW — the "incomplete MusicBrainz data" notice is not selection-gated.**
   `src/label_discover.rs:324-327` vs the `selection_ran` gate at :345. On a run aborted in the label loop *after* a cached/fresh catalogue carried incomplete payloads, the printed line reads "N release(s) skipped: incomplete MusicBrainz data" even though no selection/skipping ever happened — the count is truthful (byte-accurate about the payload) but "skipped" is a selection word applied to a discarded run. Either re-worm it ("payload could not describe N release(s)") or gate it with `selection_ran`. Cosmetic honesty nit; everything else in the aborted-run report is accurate.

### Merge verdict

18:- **Finding 1 — MEDIUM, README cache_days row is untrue for label sweeps — `README.md:332` vs `src/discography/label.rs:398`.** The README's shared `cache_days` row promises "`0` refreshes every run but keeps stale fallback." The label write path is `if config.cache_days > 0 { store_catalogue(...) }`, so with `cache_days: 0` no label row is ever written (`cache_is_fresh` is also false at `cache_days == 0`, so nothing ever becomes stale-fallback material); the artist path (`src/discography/mod.rs:1006`) writes unconditionally, so the same setting keeps stale fallback for artists only. Failure scenario: operator sets `discography.cache_days = 0`; a `--label` sweep during a MusicBrainz outage reports `Failed { kind: Provider }` and skips the label with no previous catalogue, contradicting the README and behaving differently from the artist sweep under the same option. (The design doc `docs/agent/specs/…-design.md` ("Write path: … only when `discography.cache_days > 0`") shows the gate is intentional, so the README is the operand.) Smallest fix: reword the README row ("a label sweep writes a row only when `cache_days > 0`, so `0` leaves labels without stale fallback"), or delete the guard to match the artist path.
20:- **Finding 2 — MEDIUM, README malformed-ID window off by one — `README.md:223` vs `src/discography/label.rs:144`.** README describes the refused near-miss UUID as "within three characters of a UUID's 32 digits"; the code accepts `30..=34` stripped hex digits (±2, same as `--artist`). Failure scenario: `--label 8562598d-60d1-4bd6-8b85-4d709e9517701` (35 hex digits) is not refused; it is searched as a name, fails to resolve, and a `LabelUnresolved` failure row is recorded for that non-name, replaying it as "skipped" for `failure_cache_days` — the README states a configuration error. Smallest fix: "within two characters…".
22:- **Finding 3 — LOW, docstrings contradict the shipped selection flag — `src/label_discover.rs:216-217` and `src/label_discover.rs:256-257` vs `src/runner.rs:2743`.** Both `LabelCounters::selection_ran`'s doc and `label_notices`' doc name "the library scan failed" as a case where the eligible/staged notices are withheld. The code sets `selection_ran = true` *before* the scan, so scan-failed and scan-cancelled runs do print "N album(s) eligible" and "0 staged; 0 failed" (truthful, and retaining them is right). Hazard: a maintainer "fixing" the flag's placement to satisfy the comment would change observable behaviour. Fix: drop "or the library scan failed" from both comments (withholding happens only for runs that end before `label_targets`).
24:- **Finding 4 — LOW, near-miss reason cites a shape the check does not enforce — `src/discography/label.rs:119-124` and `src/discography/label.rs:138-152`.** `looks_like_mbid` requires four hyphen-separated non-empty all-hex groups with 30-34 total hex digits but never the 8-4-4-4-12 group widths, while the refusal (and the README) claim the value "is hyphenated like a MusicBrainz ID but is not one (8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits)". A 9-4-4-4-11 spelling is refused with a rationale its groups don't meet. Refusal (never search) is correct; the parenthetical is imprecise. Fix: reword the reason/README or check group widths.
26:- **Finding 5 — LOW, `label_mbids` accepts prefix keys that can never match — `src/config.rs:266-287` (`validate_mbid_pins`) and `src/discography/label.rs:125-132` (`pinned_mbid`).** The shared validator accepts any key, so a `label_mbids` key written in the artist habit, e.g. `"mbid:8562598d-…": "other-id"`, validates as a legal pin whose folded key is `mbid:<uuid>`, while `pinned_mbid` looks a `--label` UUID input up by `normalize_catalog_key` of the bare text (no prefix) — the pin is silently dead, the run keeps asking MusicBrainz, and nothing reports why. Fix: reject label keys whose folded form carries a recognized `mbid:`/`isni:`/`ipi:` prefix (label pins are name keys only), or state the restriction in the README row.
28:- **Finding 6 — LOW, `--since` never sees an in-bound later release group of a collapsed identity — `src/label_discover.rs:108-133` with `select_albums` (`src/discography/mod.rs:593-680`).** `select_albums` keeps the earliest-dated candidate per album identity; under a `--since` bound above that date, a second release group of the same identity that satisfies the bound is never surfaced, so the album silently vanishes from the work list (its release row satisfies the bound, so it is counted under no drop reason). Only reachable when one label catalogues two release groups with identical identity and different first-release dates. Fix: a doc sentence on the SelectionCounts comment, or prefer the latest date when a bound is set.
30:- **Finding 7 — LOW, no aggregate notice for albums skipped as already processed — `src/label_discover.rs` notices (absent) and `src/runner.rs:2860-2873` (`count_label_outcome` ignores `AlbumOutcome::Skipped`).** Staged label downloads are marked success-processed (`process_album` → `finish_library_write`), so re-running the same label before the operator moves its staging copies yields "N album(s) eligible; 0 staged; 0 failed" with the only explanation in the per-album "Skipped (N)" report section; the README label section doesn't state that staged-but-unmoved albums are suppressed (and honoured as success records in every other mode). Parity with the artist sweep; fix: a `skipped` count/notice line, or one README sentence.

- Scenario: `run_label_discover_mode(client, cfg, db, &[LabelRequest { input: "8562598d-60d1-4bd6-8b85-4d709e95177".into(), mbid: None }], …)` — reachable from any library consumer of the new `pub` runner, and from any future code path that builds `LabelRequest` from config instead of clap — spends a MusicBrainz *name search* on the typo and reports it as "unresolved on MusicBrainz", i.e. exactly the behaviour the module doc and the design forbid.
- Smallest fix: classify in `from_parts` (`let parsed = LabelInput::parse(&input); match (parsed.malformed_reason(), mbid) …` → keep `Malformed`), or in the runner use `LabelInput::parse(&request.input)` when `request.mbid.is_none()`.

### Finding: MEDIUM — the round-4 empty-selection scan skip and the core's own guards are untested

- Location: `src/runner.rs:2743-2751` (the skip) and `src/runner.rs:2608-2618` (the duplicated `discography.enabled` / `library.paths` guards).
- Evidence: every label test calls `run_label_discover_mode_with_provider` with `discover_fixture(...)`, which always has a readable library root and `discography.enabled == true`. `the_release_type_override_reaches_the_selection` (`runner.rs:7553`) *does* produce an empty selection, but it only asserts that nothing was staged, so it passes with or without the skip; `a_missing_library_root_aborts_the_label_run_like_the_artist_sweep` (`runner.rs:7518`) deliberately uses a non-empty selection. `src/main.rs:1265-1298` exercises only the wrapper's guard (it returns before provider construction).
- Scenario: a later edit reintroduces the scan before the empty-selection check, or drops the core guards, and the suite stays green — while an empty-selection run against a mistyped `library.paths` flips from exit 0 to a hard error, and a direct core call with `discography.enabled = false` stops refusing.
- Smallest fix: two tests. (a) `config.library.paths = vec!["/nonexistent/library/root".into()]` plus a catalogue whose only release is a `Single` and `release_types = Some(&[Ep])` → expect `Ok(())`. (b) Call the core with `discography.enabled = false`, and with `library.paths.clear()`, and assert both `SeakarrError::Config` messages.

**Finding: HIGH — an interrupted album is still counted, budget‑charged and reported as a failure; the `Err(SeakarrError::Cancelled)` arm that was supposed to prevent this is unreachable.**
Location: `src/runner.rs:2820-2845` (Ok arm `2821-2831`, Err arm `2834-2842`).

Evidence: `SeakarrError::Cancelled` is constructed in exactly one place, the library walk (`src/scanner.rs:327`; declared `src/error.rs:27`). `process_album` never walks the library, so it can never return that variant. A Ctrl+C during a download arrives as `SeakarrError::Download("download cancelled by user")` (`src/download.rs:193, 204, 437, 473, 492, 848, 952, 1408`), which `download_ranked_candidates` deliberately swallows into `Ok(DownloadStage::Failed { outcome: AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason } })` (`runner.rs:1404-1440`), and `process_album` then returns `Ok(outcome)` (`runner.rs:706-708`).

Failure scenario: `seakarr --mode discover --label "Hospital Records"` with ten missing albums; the operator presses Ctrl+C while album 3 downloads.
1. `Ok(AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason: "download cancelled by user" })` → `charges_download_budget` is true for `Failed` (`runner.rs:2329-2334`) → `budget.charge()`;
2. `count_label_outcome` → `failed_albums += 1` (`runner.rs:2874-2887`);
3. `report.record(..., AlbumOutcome::Failed { .. })` → the summary prints `Failed (1): … download cancelled by user`;
4. next iteration sees the flag and sets `counters.cancelled = true`, so the summary reads `… 0 album(s) staged; 1 failed` plus `cancelled by user`.

So the operator is told the run failed an album it merely interrupted, `discover.max_cycle_downloads` loses one slot permanently (scheduled runs download one fewer album), and the round‑6 claim ("an interrupted album is no longer counted or reported as a failure") does not hold. Secondary aggravating detail: the budget check precedes the cancel check (`runner.rs:2798-2804`), so when the interrupted album's charge exhausts the budget the run reports `budget … reached` rather than `cancelled` — the exact conflation the artist sweep's comment at `runner.rs:3271-3275` warns about.

Smallest fix: in the `Ok(outcome)` arm, treat a failure whose reason says so as a cancellation, using the idiom already in the tree (`runner.rs:1836-1839`):
`if matches!(&outcome, AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason } if reason.contains("cancelled by user")) { counters.cancelled = true; break; }` — before charging, counting or recording. (Checking the flag alone would also convert a real failure that coincides with an interrupt, so match the reason.) Add a regression test (see next finding).

**Finding: MEDIUM — no test covers cancellation during an album, which is why the HIGH defect passed six rounds.**
Location: label test block `src/runner.rs:7420-7935`; cancel tests are only `a_cancelled_label_run_stops_before_the_first_label` (`runner.rs:7760`) and `cancellation_after_the_first_label_stops_the_sweep` (`runner.rs:7869`, which drives the between‑labels poll via `CancellingProvider`, `runner.rs:7795`).

Nothing exercises the pre‑album poll (`runner.rs:2802-2804`) or the outcome/error routes of an interrupted album, and `count_label_outcome`'s unit test (`runner.rs:7487`) asserts the very behaviour that is wrong for a cancellation. The spec's correction block (spec:449-460) claims the album path is handled. Smallest fix: one test that sets the flag inside the download stage (e.g. a `MockClient` whose write trips the flag, or a `process_album` result injected as `Failed { reason: "download cancelled by user" }`) asserting `staged_albums == 0`, `failed_albums == 0`, `cancelled == true`, and no `Failed (…)` entry in the report.

**Finding: LOW — `--label "mbid:<uuid>"` is accepted as a label *name* and aliases the ID's cache/failure key.**

Confirmed — a real HIGH: `SeakarrError::Cancelled` only comes from the library walk, so my album-loop arm is dead and a real Ctrl+C arrives as `Ok(AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason: "download cancelled by user" })`. Fixing it now.

29:**MEDIUM — 1. Spec error table contradicts the shipped `label_mbids` rule.**
32:**MEDIUM — 2. `from_parts`' `Some(mbid)` branch skips validation the module promises, and the label runner never calls `validate()`.**
35:**MEDIUM — 3. The round-7 fix is not pinned by a test that asserts the counting.**
38:**LOW — 4. `is_identifier_style_key` is dead code.**
41:**LOW — 5. Stale cache-key documentation in two places.**
44:**LOW — 6. `outcome_is_cancellation` is a substring test on a composed message.**
47:**LOW — 7. `OFFSET_PARAM` is a positional index into the query vector.**
50:**LOW — 8. A normalised credit keeps whichever spelling MusicBrainz listed first.**
58:**HIGH: 0, MEDIUM: 3, LOW: 5** — Merge verdict: **OK with notes** (fix findings 1–3 before release; 4–8 are report-only).
=== detail ===
### Findings

**MEDIUM — 1. Spec error table contradicts the shipped `label_mbids` rule.**
`docs/agent/specs/2026-11-01-label-based-discovery-design.md:420` states: *"Malformed UUID shape in `--label` **or `label_mbids`** → refuse before any request → configuration error naming the flag."* The shipped code deliberately does the opposite (`validate_mbid_pins`, config.rs:353–369, rejects only empty/duplicate keys and invalid *values*; the round-7 requirement was "`label_mbids` accepts any key again"), and README:338 documents that such a key simply never matches. Failure scenario: an operator/agent reading the spec concludes `label_mbids: {8562598d-…95177: <uuid>}` is refused at startup; it is silently accepted and silently never matches. Smallest fix: rewrite row 420 to "Malformed UUID shape in `--label` → refuse before any request; in `label_mbids` it is accepted and can never match (README documents this)".

**MEDIUM — 2. `from_parts`' `Some(mbid)` branch skips validation the module promises, and the label runner never calls `validate()`.**
`LabelInput::from_parts` (label.rs:40–46) only classifies when `mbid` is `None`; with `Some(mbid)` it lower-cases and returns `Mbid` without `valid_mbid`. `discover_label_releases_at` only checks `malformed_reason()` (label.rs:361–373), so `runner.rs:2652` builds such an input and goes straight to `provider.label_by_id("<garbage>")` (label.rs:432–434). Compare the artist path, which validates in the runner: `input.validate().map_err(SeakarrError::Config)?` (runner.rs:2008). Concrete failure: a caller of the public `run_label_discover_mode` with `LabelRequest { input, mbid: Some("not-a-uuid") }` spends a request on a garbage MBID, gets `HttpStatus(404)` → `DiscoveryFailure::Provider`, and each such label advances `consecutive_provider_failures`; three of them abort the sweep with "3 consecutive MusicBrainz failures" instead of the clean configuration error `validate()` was written to produce (label.rs:98–108). This is the case from_parts' own doc comment claims to handle ("this must not assume the value was already classified"). Smallest fix: in the `Some` branch, return `Self::parse(&mbid)` (or a `Malformed` value when `!valid_mbid`), and/or add `input.validate().map_err(SeakarrError::Config)?` before `discover_label_releases` in the runner, mirroring line 2008.

**MEDIUM — 3. The round-7 fix is not pinned by a test that asserts the counting.**
`a_cancelled_download_stops_the_label_run_without_a_failure` (runner.rs:7945–8018) asserts only that no staging folder exists and `searches == 1`. That catches the *original* bug (which let the sweep continue), but not a regression that keeps the early `break` while moving `charges_download_budget`/`count_label_outcome` above the `outcome_is_cancellation` check (runner.rs:2841–2856) — that code would still stop after one search, yet charge a budget slot, print `Failed (1):` and report `1 failed`. `RunReport::print_summary` goes through `tracing::info!` (report.rs:160–163), so the assertion is available: wrap the run in `crate::test_support::LogCapture` and assert the captured text contains `label: cancelled by user` and `0 album(s) staged; 0 failed`, and does **not** contain `Failed (`. Smallest fix: add those three assertions to the existing test.

**LOW — 4. `is_identifier_style_key` is dead code.**
Defined at label.rs:153 with a doc comment ("A label pin is matched on the folded name, so such a key could never be looked up"), and there is no call site anywhere in the repo (whole-repo grep returns only the definition). Either wire it into a startup warning in `validate_mbid_pins` (the useful behaviour its doc describes) or delete it; as a `pub` item it compiles without a warning and will silently rot.

**LOW — 5. Stale cache-key documentation in two places.**
`discography/mod.rs:148` says a `LabelUnresolved` is *"Recorded in the failure cache under `label:<key>`"*, and spec:341–342 says *"under `label:<pin_key>`"*. The code writes `label:name:<pin_key>` / `label:id:<uuid>` (label.rs:123–131). Doc-only, but this is precisely the key space round 7 changed, so it is the sentence a future reader will trust.

**LOW — 6. `outcome_is_cancellation` is a substring test on a composed message.**
`matches!(outcome, AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason } if reason.contains("cancelled by user"))` (runner.rs:2879–2881). Non-cancel failures are built as `format!("all candidates exhausted: {e}")` (runner.rs:1409–1412), and `e` can be a client-supplied `"transfer failed: {reason}"` (download.rs:1177) or `"download channel closed unexpectedly"`. A message containing the phrase would be read as the operator's interrupt: one album uncharged, uncounted, absent from the report, and the whole sweep stopped. I could not find a reachable path where that text originates from a peer, so this is report-only; the durable form is exact equality against the constructed cancel reason (or a typed `cancelled` flag threaded out of the download stage). Note it is now a third copy of the same predicate (runner.rs:1836–1838 artist path, plus download.rs).

**LOW — 7. `OFFSET_PARAM` is a positional index into the query vector.**
musicbrainz.rs:54 (`const OFFSET_PARAM: usize = 3`) is used as `query[OFFSET_PARAM] = ("offset", …)` (musicbrainz.rs:764–766). Reordering the literal at musicbrainz.rs:719–726 would overwrite a different parameter. It fails loudly (`page.count != count` or `page.offset != offset`, musicbrainz.rs:767–776) rather than silently truncating, so the comment's concern is overstated — but a named lookup or `query.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == "offset")` removes the hazard entirely.

**LOW — 8. A normalised credit keeps whichever spelling MusicBrainz listed first.**
`label_discover.rs:135` stores `release.artist_credit.clone()` on first insertion into `groups`, so two releases whose credits fold to the same key (`"Nu:Tone"` / `"nu:tone"`) give a `LabelTarget.artist` — and therefore a Soulseek query and staging folder name — that depends on payload order. The work *list* stays deterministic (identity/sort are folded), only the display/search spelling varies. `the_same_input_in_another_order_selects_the_same_work_list` (label_discover.rs:560–574) uses distinct credits per release, so it does not cover this. Smallest fix: keep the lexicographically smallest spelling for a key (`or_insert_with` → compare-and-replace) and add one test with a reordered same-credit pair.

### Notes / limitations
- No HIGH findings: I could not construct a wrong-result, data-loss, contract-break or race scenario from the diff; the round-7 fix, the key space, pins and the observability list all check out as claimed.
- Skipped reads (budget): `label.rs` tests 1251–1498 (seen only through greps), `label_discover.rs` tests 600–800 (partially), `runner.rs` label fixture 7099–7240, and the rest of `musicbrainz.rs`. None of the findings depends on those.
- Tests I did not run; the supervisor should run `cargo test` (plus `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`) to confirm the round-7 edits compile and pass — and that finding 3's proposed assertions match the real summary text.

=== eedc31f8-2e36-41ee-bd0c-fdedd55b2b4b ===
15:**MEDIUM — cancellation predicate is a spoofable substring match.** `runner.rs:2885-2887` (`reason.contains("cancelled by user")`). The reason is built from arbitrary error text (`runner.rs:1417-1421`, `"all candidates exhausted: {e}"`), and peer-advertised basenames reach that text: `expire_queue_wait` formats `"{basename} from {username} exceeded max_queue_time_secs=..."` (`download.rs:460-468`) and `queue_position_rejection` does the same (`download.rs:643`). Scenario: a peer advertises `01 - cancelled by user.flac`, never accepts the transfer, the default 1800 s queue deadline expires → `AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason: "...cancelled by user.flac..." }` → `outcome_is_cancellation` is true → the label sweep stops, reports "cancelled by user", exits 0, and the album is never counted or recorded. The unit test only pins two strings, so this false positive is untested. Smallest fix: carry a typed cancellation signal (or match the exact reason `"download cancelled by user"`), and add a `Failed` reason embedding the phrase as a negative test. (The same predicate already exists for the artist sweep at `runner.rs:1836-1839`; this diff adds a second copy of the weakness.)
17:**MEDIUM — `--since` is applied after identity collapse, silently dropping an album a release group satisfies.** `select_albums` keeps the earliest-dated release group per album identity (`discography/mod.rs:641-653`); `label_targets` then drops the target if that one date is below the bound (`label_discover.rs:154-162`). Scenario: a label lists two release groups with the same title/credit, first released 1999 and 2023; `--since 2020` should include the 2023 group, but the 1999 group becomes the identity's representative, the album is dropped, and it is **not** counted as `since_skipped` (the struct doc at `label_discover.rs:36-40` admits this). <skill name="qa-gate">
# QA Gate

**Core principle:** No code ships without passing every check. Zero tolerance for skipped gates.

**Violating the letter of these gates is violating the spirit of these gates.**

## Prerequisite: Harness and Project Context

Before beginning, ensure both prerequisites are loaded:

1. If `Harness status: loaded.` is not already present as an emitted status line, load and run `harness`, then return here.
2. If `Project context status: loaded.` is not already present as an emitted status line, load and run `get-context`,
   then return here.

When invoked from a chain, preserve these status markers and do not repeat either prerequisite.

## Upstream Workflow Barrier

Before running any gate or classifying changed languages, check for an upstream
review workflow. Use the read-only subagent fleet/status check; this does not
dispatch subagents and is allowed even though QA gates run checks directly.

- If an active reviewer workflow is present, call `bg_wait` for its exact run
  (or all of its children) and stop this skill. Do not run QA commands on a
  tree that may still change.
- If the latest emitted `REVIEW_GATE_STATUS` is `RUNNING`, stop and let the
  originating review loop emit its terminal status.
- `CLEAN` permits QA.
- `UNRESOLVED` also permits QA. The review hit its round cap and recorded its open
  findings in a residual ledger — a completion with residuals, not a failure. Run
  every gate normally, then report the ledger path and the open findings in the QA
  report. Do not fix them here.
- `BLOCKED` blocks QA: the review produced no usable result, so nothing was
  recorded and there is nothing to carry forward. Report the marker, run no gates,
  and emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED` stating that a required gate could not run.
- If no review step or review marker exists for standalone QA, continue.

## Gate Status Marker

Emit exactly one standalone status line when the gate finishes:

- `QA_GATE_STATUS: CLEAN` — every applicable gate ran and passed, or the user
  explicitly waived it and the report names the waiver.
- `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED` — any gate failed, or a required gate could not run
  and was not waived. The pre-commit prompt is asked and answered before the
  marker is emitted, so an unrun pre-commit gate reaches this marker only when
  the user stops without a waiver.

A waiver requires an answer from the user in this session: option 3 of the
pre-commit prompt, or a continuing answer to the post-failure follow-up. A
dismissed prompt, a general "carry on", or "just commit" is not a waiver.
Deciding on the user's behalf that a gate is optional is not a waiver either.

**Only an explicit user instruction to proceed anyway overrides a `FAILED` gate.**
State the failing gates and their evidence in the summary when that happens.
Nothing else overrides it — not a passing test suite, not an integration choice
already selected, not an `UNRESOLVED` review marker, and not your own judgement
that the failure is pre-existing or out of scope. `finalising` reads this marker,
so a gate that fails silently is invisible to the chain.

`finalising` requires the latest marker to be `CLEAN` before it presents
integration options, unless the user explicitly overrides a `FAILED` gate.
Never emit `CLEAN` when an applicable gate was skipped, could not run, or
reported findings. A gate recorded NOT APPLICABLE under the Missing-Tool Policy
was not skipped — state the reason in the report. A gate the user waived under
the Pre-commit Tool Flow is the only exception: it stays named in the report,
never recorded as NOT APPLICABLE.

## When to Use

**Mandatory after all code changes and before committing or creating a PR.**

Use when:

- Implementation is complete and about to commit
- About to merge to main
- About to create a PR
- Any code change is finalised

Do NOT use for:

- Mid-implementation checkpoints (use `verify` step for those)
- Design/planning phases (no code to check)
- Review-only workflows (no code changed)

## Step 0: Detect Changed Languages

Before running any gate, identify which languages were modified:

```bash
git diff --name-only HEAD
```

Classify files by language. Run ALL applicable gates for EVERY detected language.

## Language Gates

Run in order within each detected language. Report results after each gate.
Then run the Coverage Gate and Security Gate for every detected language, and
the pre-commit fallback last.

**In a chain, do NOT fix product code.** The chain scope for `qa-gate` is gates
only: report each failure, emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED`, and stop. Fixes are
re-entered through the step that owns them (code-review for lint/type errors,
the implementation step for logic). Standalone runs may fix and re-run.

Gate *configuration* problems (missing tool, unparsable config) are yours to
resolve in either mode — see Auto-Generated Configs below.

**Detect existing frameworks before enforcing new ones.** For each language, first check what the project already uses —
config files, test directories, `package.json` scripts, build tool plugins. Use the detected framework. Only fall back
to the recommended tool from the gate table below when no existing test framework is found. Do NOT force a new test
runner onto a project that already has one configured.

**Auto-generate missing tool configs.** Before running each gate, check if the tool's config file exists. If not,
generate an opinionated default from the templates below. Never overwrite an existing config. Announce each generated
config: `"⚙️ Generated default <tool> config: <filename>"`

| Tool | Config file to check | Default source |
| ------ | --------------------- | --------------- |
| ESLint (JS/TS) | `.eslintrc.*` or `eslint.config.*` | ESLint Default (below) |
| Prettier (JS/TS) | `.prettierrc*` or `prettier.config.*` | Prettier Default (below) |
| Biome (JS/TS) | `biome.json` | Biome Default (below) |
| ruff (Python) | `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml` | ruff Default (below) |

### Bash / Shell

Files matching: `*.sh`, `*.bash`, shebang `#!/bin/bash`, `#!/usr/bin/env bash`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `shellcheck $(git diff --name-only HEAD -- '*.sh' '*.bash')` |

| Type check | `mypy .` |

### JavaScript / TypeScript

Files matching: `*.js`, `*.ts`, `*.jsx`, `*.tsx`, `*.mjs`, `*.cjs`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `npx eslint .` (preferred); or `npx biome check .` (if `biome.json` preferred). Config is auto-generated if missing. |
| Format | `npx prettier --check .` (preferred); Biome users: format is included in `biome check`. Config is auto-generated if missing. |
| Tests | Detect framework: check `package.json` `scripts.test` first; then look for config files — `vitest.config.*` → `npx vitest run`, `jest.config.*` → `npx jest`, `.mocharc.*` → `npx mocha`. If none found, try `npx vitest run` as default. |

preferred test runner for new projects (10x faster than Jest, native ESM). If no test framework is configured, report:
"No JS/TS test framework detected — add tests before merging."

### Go

Files matching: `*.go`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `golangci-lint run ./...` |
| Format | `gofmt -d .` (diff mode — check only) |
| Tests | `go test ./...` |

If `golangci-lint` is not installed, fall back to `go vet ./...`. `golangci-lint` bundles 100+ linters (vet,
staticcheck, errcheck, etc.) and is the industry standard for Go.

### Rust

Files matching: `*.rs`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` |
| Format | `cargo fmt --check` |

### Coverage Gate (all detected languages)

Measure coverage fresh on the full suite with the project's detected tool; never
reuse a number from an earlier step, because code changed since then. Use the
project's configured args and tooling; these defaults apply only when no
coverage tooling exists:

| Ecosystem | Default command |
| ----------- | ----------------- |
| Python | `pytest --cov` |
| JS/TS | `npx vitest run --coverage` (Vitest) or `npx jest --coverage` (Jest) |
| Go | `go test -cover ./...` |
| Rust | `cargo llvm-cov` |
| Other | the project's standard coverage tool, with its configured threshold |

**Threshold:** the project's configured threshold (coverage config,
`--cov-fail-under`, `coverageThreshold`, and equivalents); otherwise **95%**, the
same default as the `tech-debt` skill. Enforce with the tool's own threshold
option where available (`pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=<N>`,
`coverage report --fail-under=<N>`, Vitest/Jest `coverageThreshold`). A
`--coverage <N>` override passed in `$@` replaces the default.

If the detected test command already enforces the threshold, that run satisfies
this gate; do not measure coverage twice.

**This gate fails when** reported coverage is below the threshold, or the project
configures coverage tooling that cannot run (see Missing-Tool Policy).

```bash
command -v pre-commit
```

**Installed** → run the gate below.

**Absent** → ask the user once with the harness prompt tool (see `harness`, User
Prompts), offering exactly these three options:

1. **Run ephemerally** — this session's runner becomes `uvx pre-commit`, falling
   back to `pipx run pre-commit`. Nothing is installed and `pre-commit` does not
   appear on `PATH`. The first run downloads the hook environments into the
   pre-commit cache.
2. **Install pre-commit** — `uv tool install pre-commit`, falling back to
   `pipx install pre-commit`. If neither exists, print the command for the
   user's platform and wait (`brew install pre-commit`,
   `python3 -m pip install --user pre-commit`, or the zipapp from the pre-commit
   releases page). Re-check `command -v pre-commit`; once it resolves, the runner
   is bare `pre-commit`.
3. **Skip this gate** — record the waiver and carry on with the remaining work.

Never use `sudo`, a system package manager, or the project's own environment
yourself — the printed fallback is the user's to run. Never run
`pre-commit install`: wiring git hooks is the user's call, not this gate's. If
the chosen route fails (no uv, no network, install error), say what failed and
ask once more: continue without the gate, or stop. Only an answer to that
follow-up waives the gate.

Run the prompt before you emit the gate marker — it blocks. Record the outcome
as one line in the QA report and reuse it for the rest of the session; never ask
twice.

**Waiver wording:** `SKIPPED - user waiver (pre-commit not installed)`. Name it
in the gate table and in the QA summary; `CLEAN` remains available because the
user authorised the skip.

Once a runner is selected and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` does not exist,
auto-generate the default config (see Auto-Generated Configs above) before any
hook runs. Never write a config that nothing on this machine can run.

Then run the gate with the selected runner:

```bash
<runner> run --all-files      # e.g. uvx pre-commit run --all-files
```

Use the same runner for every re-run this session.

**Do NOT commit** — this is verification only. In a chain, report failures and
stop; do NOT fix product code. Standalone runs may fix and re-run until clean.

### Auto-Detection (Languages Without Explicit Gates)

For files in languages not listed above, detect the project type from config files and run appropriate checks. Do NOT
skip to a manual review — this is an automated gate.

**Detection table — scan for these project files and run the corresponding commands:**

| Config file | Language | Test command | Lint/check command |
| ------------- | ---------- | ------------- | ------------------- |
| `package.json` | JS/TS | `npm test` | `npx eslint .` (if configured) |
| `go.mod` | Go | `go test ./...` | `golangci-lint run ./...` (fall back to `go vet ./...`) |
| `Cargo.toml` | Rust | `cargo test` | `cargo clippy` |
| `Gemfile` | Ruby | Detect: `bundle exec rspec` (if `spec/` or `.rspec` exists), else `bundle exec rake test` (minitest) | `bundle exec rubocop` |
| `pom.xml` | Java | `mvn test` | `mvn checkstyle:check` (if plugin configured) |
| `build.gradle*` | Java/Kotlin | `gradle test` | `gradle check` (if checkstyle/spotless configured) |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | C/C++ | `ctest` | `cppcheck .` (or `clang-tidy` if `compile_commands.json` exists) |
| `Makefile` | C/C++ | `make test` (if target exists) | `cppcheck .` (or `clang-tidy` if `compile_commands.json` exists) |

**Procedure:**

1. Run
   `find . -maxdepth 2 \( -name 'package.json' -o -name 'go.mod' -o -name 'Cargo.toml' -o -name 'Gemfile' -o -name 'pom.xml' -o -name 'build.gradle*' -o -name 'CMakeLists.txt' \) 2>/dev/null`
   to find project configs.
2. For each match, run the corresponding test and lint commands from the table.
3. If a tool is not installed, skip it and note the skip — but tests must still pass via whatever runner IS available.
4. If NO config file is detected at all, ask the user: "No test framework detected for changed files. Which test/lint
   commands should I run?" and wait for input. Do NOT skip to a manual review without user input.

## The Iron Law

```text
ALL GATES FOR ALL DETECTED LANGUAGES MUST PASS BEFORE PROCEEDING
```

No skipping. No "it's just a warning." No "I already ran that." Run every gate, report every result.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --------- | ----- |
| Skipping shellcheck because "it's just a script" | Shell scripts run in production. Lint them. |
| Skipping bats because "I tested manually" | Manual testing is not repeatable. Run bats. |
| Skipping ruff because "formatting is cosmetic" | Ruff catches bugs too. Run it. |
| Accepting mypy `# type: ignore` without investigation | Every ignore is a potential runtime error. Fix the type. |
| Skipping a "flaky" test | Flaky tests hide real bugs. Investigate and fix. |
| Skipping lint/format because "no config exists" | Auto-generate a default config. No gate should skip for missing config — the templates are provided in this skill. |
| Treating auto-detection as optional — "it's not in the explicit gates list" | The auto-detection table IS a gate. Run it for every detected config file. |
| Running pre-commit after committing | Run it BEFORE committing. Verification gate, not cleanup. |
| Generating `.pre-commit-config.yaml` before checking the tool | Check the tool first. A config nothing can run is a broken gate in the repo. |
| Installing software without asking, or with `sudo` / a system package manager | Offer the three options, then install only with `uv` or `pipx` on consent. |
| Only running gates for one language in a multi-language change | Every changed language gets every gate. |
| Re-using cached results from earlier | Run fresh. Cached results hide regressions. |
| Fixing product code during an in-chain QA run | QA verifies. Report the failure, emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED`, and let the owning step fix it. |
| Forcing a new test framework onto an existing project | If the project already has configured tests (config files, scripts.test, test directories), use them. Only pick a default when nothing exists. |
| Reusing the coverage number from an earlier step | Code changed since then. Measure coverage fresh on the final tree. |
| Skipping a scanner the project never configured | Run it ephemerally first (`uvx pip-audit`); only then record NOT APPLICABLE. |
| Emitting FAILED because the project never had coverage/security tooling | That is NOT APPLICABLE under the Missing-Tool Policy, not a gate failure. |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
| -------- | --------- |
| "shellcheck shows style warnings — that's fine" | ShellCheck warnings catch real bugs. Fix them. |
| "the bash script is too simple to need bats" | Simple scripts break. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "ruff shows warnings but no errors — that's fine" | Warnings become errors in CI. Fix them now. |
| "mypy only has one error, I'll skip it" | One type error = one guaranteed runtime crash path. |
| "that test is flaky, not my fault" | Your code is in the repo. Flaky tests are your problem. |
| "pre-commit would pass if I committed" | The gate is verification. Run it without committing. |
| "`uvx pre-commit` is quicker than asking" | The ephemeral route is option 1 of the prompt, not a shortcut around it. Ask first. |
| "I'll install it quietly with pip" | Install only on consent, only with `uv` or `pipx` — never `sudo`, a system package manager, or the project environment. |
| "The user is in a hurry, so I'll skip the question" | One prompt costs seconds; a silently unrun gate costs the report its credibility. |
| "`pre-commit install` is the responsible thing to do" | It writes `.git/hooks`. Wiring hooks is the user's call, not this gate's. |
| "I'll emit FAILED now and re-emit CLEAN after the user answers" | Ask first: the prompt blocks, so the marker reflects the answer. A gate waiting on a prompt you never sent is unrun, not pending. |
| "Never install a dependency to run a gate, so pre-commit must FAIL" | That rule protects the project environment. A consented `uv`/`pipx` user-tool install is the flow's option 2. |
| "A waived gate is really NOT APPLICABLE" | NOT APPLICABLE is for a tool the project never configured. A waiver is named as a waiver. |
| "I ran these in a previous step" | Code changed since then. Run them again fresh. |
| "the CI will catch this" | CI is not your personal QA gate. Run it locally. |
| "only Python files changed, I'll skip the bash gates" | You changed bash files. Run the bash gates. |
| "no config exists for X, so I'll skip that gate" | Auto-generate the default from this skill's templates. A missing config is never a valid reason to skip a gate. |
| "I'll just fix this one type error myself" | In a chain that is the code-review step's job. QA mutation hides the failure from the gate marker. |
| "Coverage is tech-debt's problem" | tech-debt fixes coverage earlier in the chain; QA verifies the final tree still meets the threshold. |
| "The dependency audit isn't one of this skill's gates" | It is now: CRITICAL/HIGH advisories fail the Security Gate. |
| "I'll route the advisory to a later step instead of failing" | Findings that meet a gate's fail conditions ARE the gate failure. Emit FAILED. |
| "The CVE can be fixed after release" | Known HIGH/CRITICAL advisories block QA. That is the point of the gate. |

## Red Flags — STOP

Cues with no matching row in Common Rationalizations:

- "cargo clippy warnings are just style — they're fine"
- "go vet warnings are informational — I'll skip them"
- "no config exists for X — I'll skip that gate" (auto-generate it instead)
- "this language isn't in the explicit gates list — I'll just do a manual review" (use auto-detection instead)
- "the project uses Jest but Vitest is faster — I'll switch it" (respect existing framework configuration)
- "no scanner is installed, so there is nothing to check"

**All of these mean: run the gate you're trying to skip. Every language, every gate, every time.**
</skill>

details.skillContent:
# QA Gate

**Core principle:** No code ships without passing every check. Zero tolerance for skipped gates.

**Violating the letter of these gates is violating the spirit of these gates.**

## Prerequisite: Harness and Project Context

Before beginning, ensure both prerequisites are loaded:

1. If `Harness status: loaded.` is not already present as an emitted status line, load and run `harness`, then return here.
2. If `Project context status: loaded.` is not already present as an emitted status line, load and run `get-context`,
   then return here.

When invoked from a chain, preserve these status markers and do not repeat either prerequisite.

## Upstream Workflow Barrier

Before running any gate or classifying changed languages, check for an upstream
review workflow. Use the read-only subagent fleet/status check; this does not
dispatch subagents and is allowed even though QA gates run checks directly.

- If an active reviewer workflow is present, call `bg_wait` for its exact run
  (or all of its children) and stop this skill. Do not run QA commands on a
  tree that may still change.
- If the latest emitted `REVIEW_GATE_STATUS` is `RUNNING`, stop and let the
  originating review loop emit its terminal status.
- `CLEAN` permits QA.
- `UNRESOLVED` also permits QA. The review hit its round cap and recorded its open
  findings in a residual ledger — a completion with residuals, not a failure. Run
  every gate normally, then report the ledger path and the open findings in the QA
  report. Do not fix them here.
- `BLOCKED` blocks QA: the review produced no usable result, so nothing was
  recorded and there is nothing to carry forward. Report the marker, run no gates,
  and emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED` stating that a required gate could not run.
- If no review step or review marker exists for standalone QA, continue.

## Gate Status Marker

Emit exactly one standalone status line when the gate finishes:

- `QA_GATE_STATUS: CLEAN` — every applicable gate ran and passed, or the user
  explicitly waived it and the report names the waiver.
- `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED` — any gate failed, or a required gate could not run
  and was not waived. The pre-commit prompt is asked and answered before the
  marker is emitted, so an unrun pre-commit gate reaches this marker only when
  the user stops without a waiver.

A waiver requires an answer from the user in this session: option 3 of the
pre-commit prompt, or a continuing answer to the post-failure follow-up. A
dismissed prompt, a general "carry on", or "just commit" is not a waiver.
Deciding on the user's behalf that a gate is optional is not a waiver either.

**Only an explicit user instruction to proceed anyway overrides a `FAILED` gate.**
State the failing gates and their evidence in the summary when that happens.
Nothing else overrides it — not a passing test suite, not an integration choice
already selected, not an `UNRESOLVED` review marker, and not your own judgement
that the failure is pre-existing or out of scope. `finalising` reads this marker,
so a gate that fails silently is invisible to the chain.

`finalising` requires the latest marker to be `CLEAN` before it presents
integration options, unless the user explicitly overrides a `FAILED` gate.
Never emit `CLEAN` when an applicable gate was skipped, could not run, or
reported findings. A gate recorded NOT APPLICABLE under the Missing-Tool Policy
was not skipped — state the reason in the report. A gate the user waived under
the Pre-commit Tool Flow is the only exception: it stays named in the report,
never recorded as NOT APPLICABLE.

## When to Use

**Mandatory after all code changes and before committing or creating a PR.**

Use when:

- Implementation is complete and about to commit
- About to merge to main
- About to create a PR
- Any code change is finalised

Do NOT use for:

- Mid-implementation checkpoints (use `verify` step for those)
- Design/planning phases (no code to check)
- Review-only workflows (no code changed)

## Step 0: Detect Changed Languages

Before running any gate, identify which languages were modified:

```bash
git diff --name-only HEAD
```

Classify files by language. Run ALL applicable gates for EVERY detected language.

## Language Gates

Run in order within each detected language. Report results after each gate.
Then run the Coverage Gate and Security Gate for every detected language, and
the pre-commit fallback last.

**In a chain, do NOT fix product code.** The chain scope for `qa-gate` is gates
only: report each failure, emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED`, and stop. Fixes are
re-entered through the step that owns them (code-review for lint/type errors,
the implementation step for logic). Standalone runs may fix and re-run.

Gate *configuration* problems (missing tool, unparsable config) are yours to
resolve in either mode — see Auto-Generated Configs below.

**Detect existing frameworks before enforcing new ones.** For each language, first check what the project already uses —
config files, test directories, `package.json` scripts, build tool plugins. Use the detected framework. Only fall back
to the recommended tool from the gate table below when no existing test framework is found. Do NOT force a new test
runner onto a project that already has one configured.

**Auto-generate missing tool configs.** Before running each gate, check if the tool's config file exists. If not,
generate an opinionated default from the templates below. Never overwrite an existing config. Announce each generated
config: `"⚙️ Generated default <tool> config: <filename>"`

| Tool | Config file to check | Default source |
| ------ | --------------------- | --------------- |
| ESLint (JS/TS) | `.eslintrc.*` or `eslint.config.*` | ESLint Default (below) |
| Prettier (JS/TS) | `.prettierrc*` or `prettier.config.*` | Prettier Default (below) |
| Biome (JS/TS) | `biome.json` | Biome Default (below) |
| ruff (Python) | `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml` | ruff Default (below) |
| mypy (Python) | `[tool.mypy]` in `pyproject.toml` | mypy Default (below) |
| pre-commit (all) | `.pre-commit-config.yaml` | pre-commit Default (below) |

When appending to `pyproject.toml`, add the section only if the table header is not already present. Do NOT duplicate
existing sections.

#### ESLint Default

```json
{
  "env": { "browser": true, "es2021": true, "node": true },
  "extends": ["eslint:recommended"],
  "parserOptions": { "ecmaVersion": "latest", "sourceType": "module" },
  "rules": {
    "no-unused-vars": ["warn", { "argsIgnorePattern": "^_" }],
    "no-console": "warn",
    "eqeqeq": ["error", "always"],
    "curly": "error"
  }
}
```

#### Prettier Default

```json
{
  "semi": true,
  "trailingComma": "all",
  "singleQuote": true,
  "printWidth": 120,
  "tabWidth": 2
}
```

#### Biome Default

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://biomejs.dev/schemas/1.9.4/schema.json",
  "organizeImports": { "enabled": true },
  "linter": { "enabled": true, "rules": { "recommended": true } },
  "formatter": { "enabled": true, "indentStyle": "space", "indentWidth": 2, "lineWidth": 120 },
  "javascript": { "formatter": { "quoteStyle": "single", "semicolons": "always" } }
}
```

#### ruff Default

```toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
```

#### mypy Default

```toml
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_unused_configs = true
strict_optional = true
```

#### pre-commit Default

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v4.6.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-added-large-files
```

### Bash / Shell

Files matching: `*.sh`, `*.bash`, shebang `#!/bin/bash`, `#!/usr/bin/env bash`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `shellcheck $(git diff --name-only HEAD -- '*.sh' '*.bash')` |
| Format | `shfmt -d .` (diff mode — check only, do not modify) |
| Tests | Detect: if `.bats` files exist anywhere → `bats -r .`; else skip and note "No bats test files found" |

If `.bats` files exist but `bats` is not installed, skip and note it. `shellcheck` is mandatory — install it if missing.

### Python

Files matching: `*.py`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint + Format | `ruff check --fix . && ruff format .` |
| Type check | `mypy .` |
| Tests | Detect framework: if `pytest` is configured (`pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest]`, `pytest.ini`, `conftest.py`) → `pytest -v`; if `tox.ini` exists → `tox`; else `python -m unittest discover` |

Pytest is the default when no framework is detected. If a different framework is already configured, respect it.

### JavaScript / TypeScript

Files matching: `*.js`, `*.ts`, `*.jsx`, `*.tsx`, `*.mjs`, `*.cjs`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `npx eslint .` (preferred); or `npx biome check .` (if `biome.json` preferred). Config is auto-generated if missing. |
| Format | `npx prettier --check .` (preferred); Biome users: format is included in `biome check`. Config is auto-generated if missing. |
| Tests | Detect framework: check `package.json` `scripts.test` first; then look for config files — `vitest.config.*` → `npx vitest run`, `jest.config.*` → `npx jest`, `.mocharc.*` → `npx mocha`. If none found, try `npx vitest run` as default. |

Configs for ESLint, Prettier, and Biome are auto-generated if missing (see Auto-Generated Configs above). Vitest is the
preferred test runner for new projects (10x faster than Jest, native ESM). If no test framework is configured, report:
"No JS/TS test framework detected — add tests before merging."

### Go

Files matching: `*.go`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `golangci-lint run ./...` |
| Format | `gofmt -d .` (diff mode — check only) |
| Tests | `go test ./...` |

If `golangci-lint` is not installed, fall back to `go vet ./...`. `golangci-lint` bundles 100+ linters (vet,
staticcheck, errcheck, etc.) and is the industry standard for Go.

### Rust

Files matching: `*.rs`

| Gate | Command |
| ------ | --------- |
| Lint | `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` |
| Format | `cargo fmt --check` |
| Tests | `cargo test` |

### Coverage Gate (all detected languages)

Measure coverage fresh on the full suite with the project's detected tool; never
reuse a number from an earlier step, because code changed since then. Use the
project's configured args and tooling; these defaults apply only when no
coverage tooling exists:

| Ecosystem | Default command |
| ----------- | ----------------- |
| Python | `pytest --cov` |
| JS/TS | `npx vitest run --coverage` (Vitest) or `npx jest --coverage` (Jest) |
| Go | `go test -cover ./...` |
| Rust | `cargo llvm-cov` |
| Other | the project's standard coverage tool, with its configured threshold |

**Threshold:** the project's configured threshold (coverage config,
`--cov-fail-under`, `coverageThreshold`, and equivalents); otherwise **95%**, the
same default as the `tech-debt` skill. Enforce with the tool's own threshold
option where available (`pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=<N>`,
`coverage report --fail-under=<N>`, Vitest/Jest `coverageThreshold`). A
`--coverage <N>` override passed in `$@` replaces the default.

If the detected test command already enforces the threshold, that run satisfies
this gate; do not measure coverage twice.

**This gate fails when** reported coverage is below the threshold, or the project
configures coverage tooling that cannot run (see Missing-Tool Policy).

### Security Gate (all detected languages)

Two fast scans. The deep OWASP/IaC/cloud review is a separate, optional audit and
is not required for this gate.

**1. Dependency audit.** Use the project's installed scanner; these defaults are
standard per-ecosystem scanners:

| Ecosystem | Preferred | Ephemeral fallback |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| Python | `pip-audit`, `safety`, `trivy` | `uvx pip-audit` |
| JS/TS | `npm audit` (or the detected package manager's audit) | none needed |
| Go | `govulncheck ./...` | `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest ./...` |
| Rust | `cargo audit` | none (requires install) |
| Other | project's configured scanner | per ecosystem |

**This gate fails when** the audit reports a CRITICAL or HIGH advisory, or an
advisory the tool does not classify. MEDIUM and LOW advisories are informational
records, not gate findings: list them in the report.

**2. Secret scan of changed files.** Run the project's configured scanner if it
has one (`gitleaks detect --source . --no-git`, `trufflehog filesystem .`, or
`detect-secrets scan`). With no scanner configured, review every changed file
against this checklist:

- Credential-named variables/constants (`key`, `secret`, `password`, `token`,
  `credential`, `auth`, `api_key`)
- Config files (`.env`, `*.yml`, `*.json`, `*.conf`, `*.ini`, `*.toml`,
  `*.properties`) and comments, where secrets survive refactors and review
- Connection strings and DSNs
- Base64-encoded blobs
- CI/CD pipelines, Dockerfiles, and IaC files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`,
  `.circleci/config.yml`, `*.tf`, CloudFormation, CDK)

**This gate fails on any confirmed secret** in the changed files. Verify
placeholders and sanitized examples before reporting, and record what was
checked.

### Missing-Tool Policy (All Gates)

Run the tool ephemerally where the ecosystem supports it (`uvx pip-audit`,
`go run ...govulncheck`). Never install a dependency to run a gate: record
`not run - tool absent` and mark that gate **NOT APPLICABLE**. The pre-commit
tool is the one exception — it may be installed with the user's consent, as an
isolated user tool, under the Pre-commit Tool Flow below.

Exception: a tool the project already configures (config file, script, CI job,
pre-commit hook) is required: failing to run it is a **FAILED** gate, unless the
user waived it under the Pre-commit Tool Flow below.

Never emit `FAILED` only because the project has never used a coverage or
security tool; never emit `CLEAN` over a configured tool you did not run.

### Fallback: Pre-commit (All Languages)

Always run last, regardless of detected languages.

#### Pre-commit Tool Flow

Check the tool before the config, on every run:

```bash
command -v pre-commit
```

**Installed** → run the gate below.

**Absent** → ask the user once with the harness prompt tool (see `harness`, User
Prompts), offering exactly these three options:

1. **Run ephemerally** — this session's runner becomes `uvx pre-commit`, falling
   back to `pipx run pre-commit`. Nothing is installed and `pre-commit` does not
   appear on `PATH`. The first run downloads the hook environments into the
   pre-commit cache.
2. **Install pre-commit** — `uv tool install pre-commit`, falling back to
   `pipx install pre-commit`. If neither exists, print the command for the
   user's platform and wait (`brew install pre-commit`,
   `python3 -m pip install --user pre-commit`, or the zipapp from the pre-commit
   releases page). Re-check `command -v pre-commit`; once it resolves, the runner
   is bare `pre-commit`.
3. **Skip this gate** — record the waiver and carry on with the remaining work.

Never use `sudo`, a system package manager, or the project's own environment
yourself — the printed fallback is the user's to run. Never run
`pre-commit install`: wiring git hooks is the user's call, not this gate's. If
the chosen route fails (no uv, no network, install error), say what failed and
ask once more: continue without the gate, or stop. Only an answer to that
follow-up waives the gate.

Run the prompt before you emit the gate marker — it blocks. Record the outcome
as one line in the QA report and reuse it for the rest of the session; never ask
twice.

**Waiver wording:** `SKIPPED - user waiver (pre-commit not installed)`. Name it
in the gate table and in the QA summary; `CLEAN` remains available because the
user authorised the skip.

Once a runner is selected and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` does not exist,
auto-generate the default config (see Auto-Generated Configs above) before any
hook runs. Never write a config that nothing on this machine can run.

Then run the gate with the selected runner:

```bash
<runner> run --all-files      # e.g. uvx pre-commit run --all-files
```

Use the same runner for every re-run this session.

**Do NOT commit** — this is verification only. In a chain, report failures and
stop; do NOT fix product code. Standalone runs may fix and re-run until clean.

### Auto-Detection (Languages Without Explicit Gates)

For files in languages not listed above, detect the project type from config files and run appropriate checks. Do NOT
skip to a manual review — this is an automated gate.

**Detection table — scan for these project files and run the corresponding commands:**

| Config file | Language | Test command | Lint/check command |
| ------------- | ---------- | ------------- | ------------------- |
| `package.json` | JS/TS | `npm test` | `npx eslint .` (if configured) |
| `go.mod` | Go | `go test ./...` | `golangci-lint run ./...` (fall back to `go vet ./...`) |
| `Cargo.toml` | Rust | `cargo test` | `cargo clippy` |
| `Gemfile` | Ruby | Detect: `bundle exec rspec` (if `spec/` or `.rspec` exists), else `bundle exec rake test` (minitest) | `bundle exec rubocop` |
| `pom.xml` | Java | `mvn test` | `mvn checkstyle:check` (if plugin configured) |

## The Iron Law

```text
ALL GATES FOR ALL DETECTED LANGUAGES MUST PASS BEFORE PROCEEDING
```

No skipping. No "it's just a warning." No "I already ran that." Run every gate, report every result.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --------- | ----- |
| Skipping shellcheck because "it's just a script" | Shell scripts run in production. Lint them. |
| Skipping bats because "I tested manually" | Manual testing is not repeatable. Run bats. |
| Skipping ruff because "formatting is cosmetic" | Ruff catches bugs too. Run it. |
| Accepting mypy `# type: ignore` without investigation | Every ignore is a potential runtime error. Fix the type. |
| Skipping a "flaky" test | Flaky tests hide real bugs. Investigate and fix. |
| Skipping lint/format because "no config exists" | Auto-generate a default config. No gate should skip for missing config — the templates are provided in this skill. |
| Treating auto-detection as optional — "it's not in the explicit gates list" | The auto-detection table IS a gate. Run it for every detected config file. |
| Running pre-commit after committing | Run it BEFORE committing. Verification gate, not cleanup. |
| Generating `.pre-commit-config.yaml` before checking the tool | Check the tool first. A config nothing can run is a broken gate in the repo. |
| Installing software without asking, or with `sudo` / a system package manager | Offer the three options, then install only with `uv` or `pipx` on consent. |
| Only running gates for one language in a multi-language change | Every changed language gets every gate. |
| Re-using cached results from earlier | Run fresh. Cached results hide regressions. |
| Fixing product code during an in-chain QA run | QA verifies. Report the failure, emit `QA_GATE_STATUS: FAILED`, and let the owning step fix it. |
| Forcing a new test framework onto an existing project | If the project already has configured tests (config files, scripts.test, test directories), use them. Only pick a default when nothing exists. |
| Reusing the coverage number from an earlier step | Code changed since then. Measure coverage fresh on the final tree. |
| Skipping a scanner the project never configured | Run it ephemerally first (`uvx pip-audit`); only then record NOT APPLICABLE. |
| Emitting FAILED because the project never had coverage/security tooling | That is NOT APPLICABLE under the Missing-Tool Policy, not a gate failure. |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
| -------- | --------- |
| "shellcheck shows style warnings — that's fine" | ShellCheck warnings catch real bugs. Fix them. |
| "the bash script is too simple to need bats" | Simple scripts break. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "ruff shows warnings but no errors — that's fine" | Warnings become errors in CI. Fix them now. |
| "mypy only has one error, I'll skip it" | One type error = one guaranteed runtime crash path. |
| "that test is flaky, not my fault" | Your code is in the repo. Flaky tests are your problem. |
| "pre-commit would pass if I committed" | The gate is verification. Run it without committing. |
| "`uvx pre-commit` is quicker than asking" | The ephemeral route is option 1 of the prompt, not a shortcut around it. Ask first. |
| "I'll install it quietly with pip" | Install only on consent, only with `uv` or `pipx` — never `sudo`, a system package manager, or the project environment. |
| "The user is in a hurry, so I'll skip the question" | One prompt costs seconds; a silently unrun gate costs the report its credibility. |
| "`pre-commit install` is the responsible thing to do" | It writes `.git/hooks`. Wiring hooks is the user's call, not this gate's. |
| "I'll emit FAILED now and re-emit CLEAN after the user answers" | Ask first: the prompt blocks, so the marker reflects the answer. A gate waiting on a prompt you never sent is unrun, not pending. |
| "Never install a dependency to run a gate, so pre-commit must FAIL" | That rule protects the project environment. A consented `uv`/`pipx` user-tool install is the flow's option 2. |
| "A waived gate is really NOT APPLICABLE" | NOT APPLICABLE is for a tool the project never configured. A waiver is named as a waiver. |
| "I ran these in a previous step" | Code changed since then. Run them again fresh. |
| "the CI will catch this" | CI is not your personal QA gate. Run it locally. |
| "only Python files changed, I'll skip the bash gates" | You changed bash files. Run the bash gates. |
| "no config exists for X, so I'll skip that gate" | Auto-generate the default from this skill's templates. A missing config is never a valid reason to skip a gate. |
| "I'll just fix this one type error myself" | In a chain that is the code-review step's job. QA mutation hides the failure from the gate marker. |
| "Coverage is tech-debt's problem" | tech-debt fixes coverage earlier in the chain; QA verifies the final tree still meets the threshold. |
| "The dependency audit isn't one of this skill's gates" | It is now: CRITICAL/HIGH advisories fail the Security Gate. |
| "I'll route the advisory to a later step instead of failing" | Findings that meet a gate's fail conditions ARE the gate failure. Emit FAILED. |
| "The CVE can be fixed after release" | Known HIGH/CRITICAL advisories block QA. That is the point of the gate. |

Cues with no matching row in Common Rationalizations:

- "cargo clippy warnings are just style — they're fine"
- "go vet warnings are informational — I'll skip them"
- "no config exists for X — I'll skip that gate" (auto-generate it instead)
- "this language isn't in the explicit gates list — I'll just do a manual review" (use auto-detection instead)
- "the project uses Jest but Vitest is faster — I'll switch it" (respect existing framework configuration)
- "no scanner is installed, so there is nothing to check"

**All of these mean: run the gate you're trying to skip. Every language, every gate, every time.**
